geometry_edits.rationale: Make the primary mass a true courtyard-bearing form so the void is programmatic rather than incidental.
Increase the carve so the public void becomes legible in all views.
Open the court toward the verified access edge to strengthen the street threshold.
Lower the connector so it reads as an entry seam and not a detached thin piece.
Trim the upper reach to restore calmer hierarchy above the ground relation.

graph_edits.rationale: Retain the compact split-wing/courtyard idea but make the void more decisive and program-bearing instead of a shallow subtraction.
Open the court further so the public middle reads as usable space rather than a decorative notch.
Align the court opening with the verified access/frontage side to strengthen the ground threshold.
Lower and broaden the connector to become a clearer entry seam rather than a thin bridge-like artifact.
Slightly reduce the upper extent so the mass reads as calmer above the public middle.
Bias the support expansion along the main bar direction to consolidate hierarchy and reduce fragmentary stepping.

rationale: The candidate reads as a compact split-wing / terrace mass with some hierarchy and a recognizable central void, so it is not random or purely box-like. However, in the four views the dominant body still feels over-fragmented and only partially resolved: the stepped pieces read more like stacked repairs than one continuous spatial rule, and the section does not clearly communicate a robust neighborhood-living logic beyond generic terracing. The blue frontage edge is acknowledged by a nearby ground response, but the access/seam is not yet strong enough to feel decisively public. Because the form is only moderately coherent across views and the section-program relationship is weak, it does not hard-pass program fit.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More campus-like and spread out than this candidate; do not over-extend the wings or dilute the compact street edge.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Winged low-rise massing around a courtyard can read as one neighborhood figure while preserving a clear communal middle.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More single-pavilion and facade-driven than the candidate; it is useful for threshold clarity, not for the stepped composition.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A simple low pavilion with a legible entry setback can support neighborhood-scale public ground without overcomplicating the section.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual: the candidate should not copy the long sloped-ribbon typology or waterfront spectacle; use only the void/terrace logic.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stepped residential massing with a carved communal void can support neighborhood living if the ground edge stays active and the section remains coherent.

warnings: The mass is coherent enough in plan but weak in section; this is a section-program failure rather than a pure silhouette issue.
Public void exists, but it is not yet clearly legible as an active street threshold on the verified frontage edge.
Avoid reading the stepped upper profile as inherently good; here it is not yet a strongly capacity-bearing terrace figure.
